text: The battery subsystem shall support operation for at least 120 minutes under nominal conditions.
During continuous discharge, the battery-case temperature shall not exceed 60 degrees Celsius.
The battery case temperature shall exceed 60 degrees Celsius before charging.
The program shall limit electrical current through the crewmember to ≤ (less than or equal to) 2 mA.
The battery subsystem should be lightweight.
Maximum allowable load: 150 N
Minimum wall thickness = 2.5 mm
The pump shall deliver no less than 12 L/min.
The pump mass shall be no more than 3.2 kg.
The output voltage shall not be less than 24 V.
The output voltage shall not be greater than 32 V.
The cabin pressure must not fall below 70 kPa.
The signal latency shall be less than 200 ms.
The controller shall respond within 5 seconds after power-on.
The unit shall operate between -40 °C and 85 °C.
The unit shall operate from 18 V to 36 V.
The bus voltage shall be 28 V ± 2 V.
The reference frequency shall be 400 Hz.
The tank shall withstand a pressure of at least 1,500 psi.
The insulation resistance shall be ≥ 10 MΩ.
The leakage current shall be ≤ 5 mA.
The sound level shall not exceed 65 dBA during normal operation.
When the vehicle is at a pressure of 10 kPa, the valve shall close.
The valve shall close under a load of 150 N.
The system shall not store crew medical data unencrypted.
The relay shall open within 50 ms, and the indicator shall illuminate within 2 s.
The hatch shall open manually and shall lock automatically.
The operator is required to confirm the abort command.
The word shall is used in this document to denote a binding requirement.
Requirements are indicated by the term "shall" throughout this standard.
Note: The contractor shall retain these records for reference.
Rationale: Crew must be able to reach the panel in an emergency.
For example, a controller must handle 10 ms interrupts.
The team may replace modules in the field.
